summary: Georgia lookout list places a tower named lexington in Oglethorpe County; no source gives its history or describes the site today.

evidence.supports: List row for lexington: Oglethorpe County, coordinates, an elevation of 763 with no unit stated, and the codes BLL-50818 and gfc-009
The list's names for towers numbered 73 and above are its own creation; this entry is number 257
evidence.quote: (For towers 73 and above, names are my creation.)

evidence.supports: The list marks some entries as historical
The list's Google map was revised on March 22, 2016
The list explains BLL-nnn codes: GFC provided coordinates for 118 towers
The list explains gfc-nnn codes: an older GFC list described the locations of 203 towers
evidence.quote: an older GFC list described the locations of 203 towers (gfc-nnn)

notes_for_editor: Only source is the tnlandforms.us Georgia list. Two web searches and one more check found no build, staffing, fire or fate history for a Lexington tower. The Eastern U.S. Lookouts page titled Lexington is a Mississippi tower (Holmes County), not this one. The NHLR Georgia index (29 registered lookouts, read from the cache) and the Eastern U.S. Lookouts Georgia directory list no Lexington tower. The list's Lexington row has an unexplained word, deer, before the codes; the story leaves it out. The list gives the elevation with no unit; the record's 232.6 m matches 763 feet. The record's GFC US 9 is the list's gfc-009 with the zero dropped, so it is not a correction. A search result for a proposed 199-ft telecom monopole in Lexington is not a lookout and is not used. Story is about 155 words because the evidence is thin. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the page explains the BLL-nnn and gfc-nnn codes, which the story now says.
